psychology: Jakob's Law - reuses Finder's learned icon-grid + filename convention so the drawer is instantly legible; the notch-hover trigger is the deliberate product-level innovation (be conventional about UI, innovative about product)
Fitts's Law - the display notch is a fixed top-edge anchor (effectively infinite target along the edge), a strong acquisition point; the small bottom glyphs are the low-Fitts weak spot
Hick's Law - only 3 source tabs keeps the scope decision tiny
Von Restorff / signal-detection - one selected tab breaks the row pattern, but the neutral-gray selection makes the single-focus signal quiet
Aesthetic-Usability Effect - the polished composite (halo) raises perceived usability before first use
